newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares leap 2.06 pct on new govt prospect.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares leap 2.06 pct on new govt prospect.

text.p: Istanbul shares jumped on Wednesday amid liquidity inflow prompted by the rising prospect of a new secularist alliance to replace the ruling Islamist-led coalition government, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,437, up 29 points or 2.06 percent from Tuesday, but eased from an afternoon high of 1,446 due to resistance. Trade volume leapt to 16.31 trillion lira ($118.7 million) from 10.92 trillion ($79.7 million) on Tuesday.
"Buying continued from Tuesday amid expectations of a new government, but there is caution," said Alp Tekince, general manager of Bumerang securities.
The index regained 0.93 percent on Tuesday after losing 8.9 percent amid political fears since the market's opening on April 24 after a 6-1/2 day holiday to Monday's 1,395 close.
"The market will remain cautious and may move either way until a planned censure motion takes place," Tekince said.

Former minister Yalim Erez from the conservative True Path Party (DYP) held a second round of talks with two opposition leaders on Tuesday on forming a secularist pact to exclude the ruling Islamist Welfare Party (RP).
A conservative and a left-wing opposition leader said on Tuesday they fully agreed on the new coalition proposal which Erez said would aim to rule rather than hold early elections.
Erez who is expected to meet a second left-wing leader this week, said he would also discuss the plan with deputy Prime Minister and DYP leader Tansu Ciller as soon as possible.
It is not clear how many DYP deputies will support Erez's move but conservative opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz has said there was support within the party.
Erez said the opposition planned to file a censure motion to topple the government if the DYP did not pull out of the government.
